claims.claim_text: ELISA analysis of serum from 56 vaccinated individuals showed anti-spike IgG binding antibody titres increased after primary vaccination (day 0) and were significantly boosted after the secondary vaccination (day 21).

source.quote: Primary vaccination induced binding antibody and neutralizing antibody responses in all but three individuals; these responses were boosted significantly after the secondary vaccination ( Fig. 1a , b , Extended Data Fig. 1b – d ).

claims.claim_text: Bulk RNAseq analysis of whole blood from 31 participants showed the secondary vaccination (day 21) generated a greater transcriptional response than primary vaccination (day 0), with nearly a fourfold increase in differentially expressed genes at day 22 versus day 1 and induction of dendritic cell activation, Toll-like receptor signalling, monocyte and neutrophil modules on days 22 and 23 versus day 21.

source.quote: Next, we performed bulk mRNA sequencing of whole blood from 31 participants.

claims.claim_text: CITEseq assay analysis of PBMCs from 45 samples from 6 individuals showed that cluster C8, expressing CD14, VCAN, CD1C, FCGR1A and CD274 and interferon-stimulated genes including WARS, GBP1, IFI30 and IFITM3, emerged one day after secondary vaccination (day 22) and increased from about 0.01% one day after primary vaccination (day 1) to about 1%, nearly 100-fold higher.

source.quote: We performed cellular indexing of transcriptomes and epitopes by sequencing (CITE-seq) of 45 peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) samples from 6 individuals ( Extended Data Fig. 1a ) to disentangle these two effects and to examine transcriptional changes at the single-cell level.

claims.claim_text: CyTOF analysis of whole blood from 27 individuals showed the frequency of intermediate monocytes (CD14+ CD16+ monocytes) increased significantly two days after the primary vaccination (day 2) and was substantially higher two days after the secondary vaccination (day 23).

source.quote: We first assessed whole-blood samples of 27 individuals using cytometry by time of flight (CyTOF).

claims.claim_text: Flow Cytometry analysis of blood PBMCs from 38 individuals showed spike-specific CD4 and CD8 T cell responses were more readily detectable seven days after the secondary immunization (day 28) than at earlier time points.

source.quote: Vaccination also stimulated spike-specific T cell responses, which were more readily detectable seven days after the secondary immunization ( Fig. 1d , e , Extended Data Fig. 2a – e ).

claims.claim_text: Neutralizing Antibody Titer Assay analysis of serum from vaccinated individuals showed neutralizing antibody responses against the B.1.351 variant at day 42 were about tenfold lower than against the wild-type WA1/2020 strain.

source.quote: BNT162b2 vaccination also induced a neutralizing antibody response against the B.1.351 variant of concern, albeit at a tenfold-lower magnitude than against the wild-type WA1/2020 (WA1) strain ( Fig. 1c , Extended Data Fig. 1f ), consistent with previous studies 11 .

claims.claim_text: Olink assay analysis of plasma from 31 vaccinated individuals showed IFNγ and CXCL10 increased significantly on days 1 and 2 after primary vaccination (days 1 and 2) versus baseline and increased even further after the secondary immunization (day 21), with plasma IFNγ 11.3-fold higher at day 22 than at day 1.

source.quote: To further investigate this phenomenon, we measured plasma cytokines in 31 vaccinated individuals using Olink ( https://www.olink.com/products/target/inflammation/ ).
